Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: Ilww.u.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 36 s. 2023 HAY 04 2023 JAYZEL GRAFIL jayzelgrafil@gmail.com Palawan, Philippines Dear Ms. Grafil: This has reference to your letter dated January 18, 2023 to this Department requesting for guidance on the legality of a working permit imposed by one of the towns in Palawan. Per your representation, the amount of One Thousand Pesos (Php 1, 000.00) is levied yearly against every working individual even against minimum wage earners. Hence, due to the rising prices of commodities, you have brought the matter before this Department. First of all, we recognize the raised sentiments and we sympathize with every minimum wage earner fighting through the current world inflation. In order to address your inquiry, we put into light what the 1987 Constitutionl and the Local Government Code provides. Both laws provide that local government units (LGUs) have the power to create their own sources of revenue. In accordance with this power, different taxes are imposed by LGUs. However, our appreciation of the phrase "payment of working permit' pertains to Community Tax as provided in the Local Government Code of 1991 (LGC), viz: Section 156. Community Tax. - Cities or municipalities may levy a community tax in accordance with the provisions of this Article. SEC. 157. Individuals Liable to Community Tax. - Every inhabitant of the Philippines eighteen (18) years of age or over who has been regularly employed on a wage or salary basis for at least thirty (30) consecutive working days during any calendar year, or who is engaged in business or occupation, or who owns real property with an aggregate assessed value of One thousand pesos (P=l ,000.00) or more, or who is required by law to file an income tax return shall pay an annual community tax of Five pesos (P=5.00) and an annual additional tax of One peso (P=I.OO) for every One thousand pesos (P=I ,OOO.OO) of income regardless of whether from business, exercise of 1 Article X, Section 5. Each local government unit shall have the power to create its own sources of revenues and to levy taxes, fees and charges subject to such guidelines and limitations as the Congress may provide, consistent with the basic policy of local autonomy. Such taxes, fees. and charges shall accrue exclusively to the local governments. "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

profession or from property which in no case shall exceed Five thousand pesos In the case of husband and wife, the additional tax herein imposed shall be based upon the total property owned by them and the total gross receipts or earnings derived by them. As to the amount collected, the same must be based on annual community tax of Five pesos (P=5.00) and an annual additional tax of One peso (P=l .00) for every One thousand pesos (P=l ,000.00) of income. Thus, the Community Tax should be based from the salary/income. The Phpl ,000.00 collected may be unjust and unreasonable, depending on the salary/income. Be that as it may, if the "working permit" mentioned herein does not pertain to Community Tax, then we believe that the same is not authorized under the LGC. This opinion shall be without prejudice to any contrary opinion rendered by more competent authorities and/or the courts. We hope to have assisted you on the matter. Thank you very much.
